response: {"turns":[{"id":"M1:T61","text":"So you want ease of maintenance considered in both the design and the installation of the radio equipment, right?"},{"id":"M1:T62","text":"Yes, exactly."},{"id":"M1:T63","text":"For the Cab radios we should have an emergency power supply, so if the train's main power supply fails, the driver's radio can keep running for 6 hours. That's based on the cycle described in section 4.5.21."},{"id":"M1:T64","text":"And the Cab radio has to pass the electrical tests defined in IEC 571, parts 1, 2 and 3."},{"id":"M1:T65","text":"Okay, got it."},{"id":"M1:T66","text":"Let's move on to the public address interface. What do we need there?"},{"id":"M1:T67","text":"If we implement it at all, the Public Address interface should comply with the UIC Fiche, UIC 568."},{"id":"M1:T68","text":"Right."},{"id":"M1:T69","text":"What about other interfaces?"},{"id":"M1:T70","text":"Wherever other data interfaces are implemented, they should follow the RS422 standard."},{"id":"M1:T71","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T72","text":"And on the environmental and physical side, anything else?"},{"id":"M1:T73","text":"General purpose radios need rechargeable batteries that give at least eight hours of operation on a single charge, across a temperature range of +18°C to +25°C. Again, that's based on the cycle in section 4.5.21."},{"id":"M1:T74","text":"Let's talk about the numbering plan requirements."},{"id":"M1:T75","text":"All the Train Function Numbers and their associated MSISDN numbers have to sit in the same routing database, and that's the database of whatever GSM-R network the train is currently operating in."},{"id":"M1:T76","text":"Mm-hm, okay."},{"id":"M1:T77","text":"For coaches it's different. The Coach Function Number or numbers and the associated MSISDN numbers must always be stored as an entry in the routing database of the coach's home GSM-R network."},{"id":"M1:T78","text":"Also, implementing the EIRENE numbering plan must not stop any authorised caller from using the MSISDN number if they know it. That way mobiles can be assigned to particular personnel where that makes sense."},{"id":"M1:T79","text":"And how should national EIRENE numbers be used?"},{"id":"M1:T80","text":"Every railway network should treat a number as a National EIRENE Number, an NEN, unless it's preceded by an International Code that identifies another GSM-R network."}]}
